2º de Bachillerato · Inglés II

Conditionals, wishes and unreal past

Ficha para imprimir
123456
1

Pregunta de arranquePiensa 30 segundos antes de seguir

¿Por qué en «If I had a car» se usa un pasado, si estoy hablando de ahora?

Escribe o di en voz alta tu respuesta. Después .

Porque en inglés el pasado no solo marca tiempo: también marca distancia de la realidad. If I had a car significa «no tengo coche, pero imaginemos que sí». Cuanto más «hacia atrás» va el verbo, más irreal es la situación: presente para lo posible, past simple para lo irreal ahora, past perfect para lo imposible en el pasado. Ese mismo pasado irreal aparece en I wish I knew, It's time we left o I'd rather you stayed.

2

Aprende12 apartados

Para empezar: Sliding doors

In 2009 a young Spanish engineer called Marta missed her train to Barcelona by just thirty seconds. If she had caught it, she would have arrived on time for a job interview at a big company. Instead, she sat in a café, started talking to a stranger and ended up working with him on a small start-up that recycles plastic from the sea.

«People often ask me if I regret it», she says. «Honestly, if I had got that job, I would probably be sitting in an office now, and I wouldn't have travelled half the world. Of course, I sometimes wish I had more free time, and if only I had saved more money at the beginning! But provided that we keep growing, I'm happy.»

«Imagine you could go back», a journalist asked her. «Would you run faster?» Marta laughed. «Had I run faster, I would never have met my partner. So no. It's time people stopped thinking that one missed train can ruin your life.»

La historia juega con condicionales, deseos e hipótesis sobre el pasado y el presente, el contenido de este tema.

3.1 Lo real y lo irreal: la lógica de las condicionales

Una oración condicional une una condición (if-clause) y una consecuencia (main clause). Lo que decide el tipo no es el tiempo cronológico, sino lo real o irreal que el hablante considera la condición.

TipoCondiciónConsecuenciaIdea
Zeropresentpresentverdad general
Firstpresentwill / modal + basefuturo posible
Secondpast simple / werewould / could / might + baseirreal presente o futuro improbable
Thirdpast perfectwould / could / might have + participiopasado imposible

Elegir el tipo cambia el mensaje. If I win the scholarship, I'll study in Boston: lo veo posible. If I won the scholarship, I'd study in Boston: lo veo poco probable. If I had won the scholarship, I would have studied in Boston: no lo gané.

Dos reglas que no fallan: en la condición no se usa will ni would (salvo los usos especiales del apartado siguiente), y si la condición va primero, se separa con coma. Con estas bases, el resto del tema son variaciones sobre la misma lógica de «más pasado = más irreal».

3.2 Zero y first conditional: variantes avanzadas

En el zero conditional if equivale a when / whenever: If you press this button, the machine stops. En la consecuencia puede ir un imperativo: If you feel dizzy, sit down.

En el first conditional la consecuencia admite cualquier forma de futuro o modal: If it rains, we're going to cancel the match. If you finish early, you can leave. If you want to pass, you should start now. En la condición pueden aparecer el present continuous o el present perfect: If you're going to the shop, could you get some bread? If you've finished, you may go.

Hay tres usos de la condición que parecen excepciones. If + will / would cuando expresa voluntad o cortesía: If you will follow me, I'll show you to your room. I'd be grateful if you would reply soon. If + should para una posibilidad poco probable, en registro formal: If you should see Ana, give her my regards. Y if + happen to con la misma idea: If you happen to pass by, drop in.

En los writings formales es útil la fórmula de cortesía I would appreciate it if you could…, que mezcla condicional y modal para pedir algo con educación.

3.3 Second conditional y were to

El second conditional (if + past simple, would + base) expresa situaciones irreales en el presente o improbables en el futuro: If I had more time, I would learn to play the piano. If I won the lottery, I'd travel round the world.

Con el verbo be se usa were para todas las personas en registro formal: If I were you, I'd accept. If he was / were here, he'd know what to do. En los exámenes, were es siempre la opción más segura.

En la consecuencia, could y might sustituyen a would para expresar capacidad o posibilidad: If we left now, we could catch the last train. If you asked her, she might say yes. La forma continua describe una situación en curso: If I weren't studying, I'd be at the beach.

Were to + base presenta una hipótesis muy improbable o la plantea con cortesía: If the government were to raise taxes, there would be protests. If you were to move the table, we'd have more space. Es un recurso de nivel C1 que funciona muy bien en los ensayos para plantear escenarios.

3.4 Third conditional

El third conditional (if + past perfect, would have + participio) imagina un pasado distinto del real; por eso es imposible: If we had left earlier, we wouldn't have missed the plane (salimos tarde y lo perdimos).

Con could have y might have se expresa capacidad o posibilidad en ese pasado imaginado: If you had asked me, I could have helped you. If she had trained harder, she might have won.

Las formas continuas resaltan la duración: If I hadn't been driving so fast, I wouldn't have had the accident. If it had been snowing, we would have stayed at home.

Cuidado con las contracciones: en If I'd known, I'd have come, el primer 'd es had (va con participio) y el segundo es would (va con have). Un error frecuente es usar would have en la condición: *If I would have known. En la PAU es un fallo que se penaliza siempre.

Para reescribir un hecho pasado como third conditional, se invierte la polaridad: I didn't study, so I failed → If I had studied, I wouldn't have failed.

3.5 Condicionales mixtos

Cuando la condición y la consecuencia se refieren a momentos distintos, se mezclan los tipos. Hay dos combinaciones.

Pasado → presente (if + past perfect, would + base): una condición pasada imposible con una consecuencia en el presente. If I had accepted that job, I would be living in London now. If she hadn't broken her leg, she would be playing in the final today.

Presente → pasado (if + past simple, would have + participio): una característica permanente o una situación actual explica algo que pasó (o no pasó). If I weren't so shy, I would have spoken to her at the party. If he spoke English, he would have got the job.

Para identificarlos, busca las expresiones temporales: now, today, still apuntan al presente; yesterday, last year, at the party, al pasado. If I had studied medicine (pasado), I would be a doctor now (presente).

Los condicionales mixtos son un recurso excelente para reflexionar sobre la propia vida en un writing o en una presentación oral, y en la PAU aparecen en ejercicios de reescritura como: I didn't sleep last night, so I'm tired → If I had slept last night, I wouldn't be tired now.

Vídeo: 12 ways to use advanced conditionals in English · English with Greg (YouTube) · 144 mil visualizaciones

3.6 Alternativas a if

Un texto de nivel avanzado no repite if. Estas conjunciones aportan matices distintos:

ConectorSignificadoEjemplo
unlessa menos que (= if… not)Unless you hurry, you'll miss it.
provided / providing (that)siempre que (condición única)I'll lend it to you provided you return it.
as / so long assiempre que, mientrasAs long as you're careful, it's safe.
on condition thatcon la condición de que (formal)You can go on condition that you call us.
in casepor si acaso (precaución)Take a coat in case it gets cold.
suppose / supposing / what ifimagina que…Suppose you lost your job, what would you do?
even ifaunque (condición hipotética)I wouldn't tell you even if I knew.
otherwise / or elsede lo contrarioHurry, otherwise we'll be late.

Tres trampas: unless ya es negativo (*Unless you don't study es incorrecto); in case no significa «si» (I'll take an umbrella in case it rains: lo llevo ahora, llueva o no); y even if (condición) no es igual que even though (hecho real): Even though it's raining, we're going out (está lloviendo).

Con unless, provided o in case se siguen las mismas reglas de tiempos que con if: presente para el futuro.

3.7 La inversión condicional

En registro formal se puede omitir if e invertir el orden de sujeto y auxiliar. Solo funciona con tres auxiliares:

Con ifCon inversión
If I had known, I would have told you.Had I known, I would have told you.
If you should need help, call us.Should you need help, call us.
If I were in your position, I'd resign.Were I in your position, I'd resign.
If the company were to close, …Were the company to close, …

La negativa no se contrae: Had I not seen it, no *Hadn't I seen it. Should you not wish to continue, please press cancel.

But for + sustantivo equivale a «si no hubiera sido por»: But for your help, I would have failed. Con el mismo significado: If it hadn't been for / Had it not been for your help… y, en presente, If it weren't for / Were it not for the internet, we couldn't work from home.

Estas estructuras son frecuentes en cartas y correos formales (Should you have any questions, do not hesitate to contact me) y dan a un writing un registro claramente avanzado. Úsalas con moderación: una o dos por texto bastan.

Vídeo: Inversión: «Si hubiera sabido…», «Si necesitaras…» · Adam's English Lessons · engVid (YouTube) · 1,1 millones de visualizaciones

3.8 Wish e if only

Wish e if only (más enfático) expresan deseos sobre situaciones que no son como querríamos. El tiempo verbal «retrocede» igual que en las condicionales:

EstructuraSe refiere aEjemplo
wish + past simple / weredeseo sobre el presenteI wish I were taller. If only I had more time!
wish + couldcapacidad que no tenemosI wish I could speak Japanese.
wish + past perfectarrepentimiento sobre el pasadoI wish I hadn't said that.
wish + wouldqueja sobre el comportamiento de otroI wish you would stop interrupting me.

Wish + would solo se usa cuando el sujeto es distinto del que desea y se trata de algo que podría cambiar: I wish it would stop raining, pero no *I wish I would be taller.

No confundas wish con hope: hope se usa para deseos posibles y va con presente o futuro: I hope you pass (no *I wish you pass). Con un sustantivo, wish sí aparece en fórmulas: I wish you a happy birthday.

Reescrituras típicas: I regret not studying harder → I wish I had studied harder. It's a pity I can't drive → I wish I could drive. Stop making that noise! → I wish you would stop making that noise.

Vídeo: Wish / if only · RockYourEnglish (YouTube) · 423 mil visualizaciones

3.9 El pasado irreal: would rather, it's time y as if

Otras estructuras usan el mismo pasado irreal para hablar del presente o del futuro.

Would rather (preferir): con el mismo sujeto va seguido de la base (I'd rather stay at home); con un sujeto distinto, de past simple (I'd rather you stayed at home) o de past perfect para el pasado (I'd rather you hadn't told him). Would sooner funciona igual. Compárese con prefer: I'd prefer you to stay.

It's time / It's high time / It's about time + sujeto + past simple expresa que algo debería estar ocurriendo ya, a menudo con crítica: It's high time the government did something about housing. Con infinitivo, sin crítica: It's time to go.

As if / as though + pasado irreal indica que algo parece verdad pero no lo es: He talks as if he were the boss (no lo es). Con presente, si puede ser verdad: It looks as if it's going to rain.

Suppose / supposing / imagine también admiten el pasado irreal: Suppose you lost your phone. What would you do? Todas estas estructuras son muy frecuentes en las reescrituras de la PAU.

3.10 Condiciones implícitas

A veces la condición no aparece con una conjunción, sino escondida en otra palabra o en el contexto. Reconocerlas es importante para la comprensión lectora.

With / without + sustantivo: Without your support, I wouldn't have finished (= if you hadn't supported me). With a bit more effort, you could pass. Otherwise: I was ill; otherwise I would have come (si no hubiera estado enfermo). But con un modal: I would have called you, but I lost my phone.

Expresiones reducidas: if necessary, if possible, if so, if not, if in doubt, if anything. Fill in the form and, if necessary, attach a copy of your ID. Is it urgent? If so, call me. If anything, the situation has got worse (más bien).

En el habla, la condición se sobreentiende a menudo: I wouldn't do that (= if I were you). It would be great to see you (= if you came). Who would have thought it? (= if someone had asked us).

Saber «desplegar» estas condiciones ayuda a responder preguntas de comprensión del tipo «What would have happened if…?» y a reescribir frases con but for o without.

3.11 Condicionales para persuadir y ser cortés

Las condicionales son una herramienta comunicativa, no solo gramatical. En la negociación y la persuasión: If you lower the price, we'll buy two. If we invested in renewable energy, we would create thousands of jobs.

En la cortesía, el segundo condicional suaviza peticiones y opiniones: Would it be possible to change the date? It would be better if we met on Monday. I'd suggest that you contact the manager. En un correo formal: I would be grateful if you could send me further information.

En el ensayo argumentativo, el second y el third conditional permiten plantear escenarios y consecuencias: If public transport were free, fewer people would use their cars. Had the government acted earlier, the crisis could have been avoided. Una cadena de condicionales da fuerza al argumento.

En el discurso oral, las hipótesis enganchan al público: What would you do if you had just one week to live? Imagine you woke up in 1925… Usa estas preguntas para empezar una presentación o un debate.

3.12 Las condicionales en la PAU

Las reescrituras con condicionales son de las más frecuentes en la prueba. Sigue este método: 1) identifica si la frase original habla de presente, pasado o ambos; 2) invierte la polaridad (afirmativo ↔ negativo); 3) retrocede un tiempo; 4) revisa la puntuación y las contracciones.

OriginalReescritura
I don't have a car, so I can't drive you.If I had a car, I could drive you.
He didn't train, so he lost.If he had trained, he wouldn't have lost.
I didn't sleep, so I'm tired now.If I had slept, I wouldn't be tired now.
You'll fail if you don't study.Unless you study, you'll fail.
I regret buying this phone.I wish I hadn't bought this phone.
If you need anything, call me.Should you need anything, call me.
Your help saved me.But for your help, I would have failed.

Errores que más restan: will o would en la condición, doble negación con unless, olvidar la coma, confundir wish y hope y escribir would of en lugar de would have.

En el writing, una o dos condicionales bien elegidas (un were to, una inversión, un mixto) demuestran nivel. Más vale una estructura correcta que tres arriesgadas con errores.

Ejemplos resueltos

Ejemplo 1. Reescribe: «I don't know her number, so I can't call her.»

  1. Situación presente irreal.
  2. Second conditional con could e invirtiendo la polaridad.

Resultado: If I knew her number, I could call her.

Ejemplo 2. Reescribe: «I didn't take the medicine, so I'm still ill.»

  1. Causa pasada, efecto presente (still).
  2. Mixto: if + past perfect, would + base.

Resultado: If I had taken the medicine, I wouldn't be ill now.

Ejemplo 3. Reescribe con inversión: «If I had realised it was so late, I would have left.»

  1. Third conditional en registro formal.
  2. Had + sujeto + participio.

Resultado: Had I realised it was so late, I would have left.

Ejemplo 4. Reescribe con but for: «If the lifeguard hadn't been there, the boy would have drowned.»

  1. Condición negativa con un sustantivo.
  2. But for + sustantivo, consecuencia en third conditional.

Resultado: But for the lifeguard, the boy would have drowned.

Ejemplo 5. Reescribe: «I regret not going to the concert.» → «I wish ___.»

  1. Arrepentimiento sobre el pasado.
  2. Wish + past perfect, polaridad invertida.

Resultado: I wish I had gone to the concert.

Ejemplo 6. Completa: «It's high time you ___ (start) looking for a job.»

  1. It's high time + sujeto + pasado irreal.
  2. Past simple.

Resultado: It's high time you started looking for a job.

Errores típicos

  • Usar would en la condición: *If I would have time → If I had time.
  • Usar would have en el third conditional: *If I would have known → If I had known.
  • Doble negación con unless: *Unless you don't hurry → Unless you hurry.
  • Confundir wish y hope: *I wish you get the job → I hope you get the job.
  • Usar wish + would con el mismo sujeto: *I wish I would be rich → I wish I were rich.
  • Escribir would of por would have: *I would of come → I would have come.

PracticaResponde sin mirar arriba. Equivocarse aquí también enseña.

Ejercicios (32)

Hazlos en tu cuaderno y después abre la solución.

Nivel básico

  1. Completa: «If you ___ (heat) ice, it ___ (melt).»

    Ver solución
    heat, melts: zero conditional.

  2. Completa: «If it ___ (be) sunny tomorrow, we ___ (go) hiking.»

    Ver solución
    is, will go: first conditional.

  3. Completa: «If I ___ (be) you, I ___ (apologise).»

    Ver solución
    were, would apologise: consejo.

  4. Completa: «If she ___ (study), she ___ (pass) the exam last week.»

    Ver solución
    had studied, would have passed: third conditional.

  5. Completa con unless: «You won't improve ___ you practise.»

    Ver solución
    unless: a menos que practiques.

  6. Completa: «Take your phone ___ you get lost.»

    Ver solución
    in case: precaución.

  7. Completa: «I wish I ___ (can) fly.»

    Ver solución
    could: capacidad que no tenemos.

  8. Completa: «I wish I ___ (not / eat) that pizza.»

    Ver solución
    hadn't eaten: arrepentimiento.

  9. Elige hope o wish: «I ___ you have a great time in Rome.»

    Ver solución
    hope: deseo posible.

  10. Completa: «I'd rather ___ (stay) at home tonight.»

    Ver solución
    stay: mismo sujeto, base.

  11. Corrige: «If I will see him, I tell him.»

    Ver solución
    If I see him, I'll tell him.

  12. Traduce: «Si hubiera sabido la verdad, no habría venido.»

    Ver solución
    If I had known the truth, I wouldn't have come.

Nivel medio

  1. Reescribe: «She is not tall enough, so she can't be a model.»

    Ver solución
    If she were taller, she could be a model.

  2. Reescribe: «We got lost because we didn't have a map.»

    Ver solución
    If we had had a map, we wouldn't have got lost.

  3. Completa el mixto: «If I ___ (not / miss) the bus, I ___ (be) at home now.»

    Ver solución
    hadn't missed, would be.

  4. Completa el mixto: «If he ___ (be) more organised, he ___ (not / forget) the meeting yesterday.»

    Ver solución
    were (was), wouldn't have forgotten: rasgo presente, consecuencia pasada.

  5. Reescribe con provided that: «You can borrow my bike, but you must bring it back tonight.»

    Ver solución
    You can borrow my bike provided (that) you bring it back tonight.

  6. Reescribe con otherwise: «If you don't leave now, you'll miss the train.»

    Ver solución
    Leave now; otherwise you'll miss the train.

  7. Completa: «I wish my brother ___ (stop) taking my clothes.»

    Ver solución
    would stop: queja sobre otra persona.

  8. Completa: «I'd rather you ___ (not / smoke) in the car.»

    Ver solución
    didn't smoke: sujeto distinto + past simple.

  9. Completa: «He spends money as if he ___ (be) a millionaire.»

    Ver solución
    were (was): no lo es.

  10. Explica la diferencia: «even if» / «even though».

    Ver solución
    Even if introduce una condición hipotética; even though, un hecho real. Even though it's cold, we'll go (hace frío). Even if it's cold, we'll go (puede que haga frío).

  11. Completa con were to: «If the volcano ___ erupt, the village would be evacuated.»

    Ver solución
    were to: hipótesis muy improbable.

  12. Reescribe: «It's a pity I can't come to your wedding.» → «I wish ___.»

    Ver solución
    I wish I could come to your wedding.

Nivel avanzado

  1. Reescribe con inversión: «If you should require further assistance, please contact us.»

    Ver solución
    Should you require further assistance, please contact us.

  2. Reescribe con inversión: «If it weren't for the internet, I couldn't work from home.»

    Ver solución
    Were it not for the internet, I couldn't work from home.

  3. Reescribe con inversión negativa: «If I hadn't seen it, I wouldn't have believed it.»

    Ver solución
    Had I not seen it, I wouldn't have believed it.

  4. Reescribe: «Without your advice, I would have made a terrible mistake.» con if.

    Ver solución
    If it hadn't been for your advice (If you hadn't advised me), I would have made a terrible mistake.

  5. Escribe dos frases para un ensayo sobre la vivienda con were to y una inversión.

    Ver solución
    Modelo: If rents were to keep rising, young people would be unable to leave home. Had governments built more social housing, the crisis would not be so severe today.

  6. Completa: «It's about time the council ___ (do) something about the traffic. If only they ___ (listen) to us years ago!»

    Ver solución
    did, had listened.

  7. Corrige los cinco errores: «If I would know the answer, I will tell you. Unless you don't come, I won't go. I wish you pass. I would of helped you if you asked me yesterday.»

    Ver solución
    If I knew the answer, I would tell you; Unless you come, I won't go; I hope you pass; I would have helped you if you had asked me yesterday.

  8. Escribe un párrafo de 70 palabras sobre una decisión importante de tu vida con third conditional, un mixto y wish.

    Ver solución
    Modelo: Four years ago I chose to study at this school instead of the one near my house. If I had stayed in my neighbourhood, I wouldn't have met my best friends. I might also be studying humanities now instead of science. Sometimes I wish I had more free time, but I'm sure I made the right decision.

¿Has nombrado estas ideas?
★

Situación de aprendizajeWhat if? Una charla sobre decisiones

Para la jornada de orientación universitaria, cada grupo preparará una charla de cinco minutos titulada «What if?» sobre decisiones importantes (elegir carrera, estudiar fuera, emprender) con historias reales o inventadas y consejos para los compañeros.

Pasos

  1. Elegid una decisión y buscad o inventad dos historias con finales distintos.
  2. Escribid una cadena de consecuencias con third conditional y condicionales mixtos.
  3. Añadid una parte de consejos con alternativas a if (provided that, unless, in case).
  4. Incluid una reflexión con wish, if only e it's high time.
  5. Ensayad y presentad la charla con una pregunta hipotética para el público.

Producto final: Charla de cinco minutos con guion escrito y apoyo visual.

Cómo se valora

  • Usa correctamente los cuatro tipos de condicionales y al menos un mixto.
  • Emplea alternativas a if, inversión o but for con corrección.
  • Expresa deseos y arrepentimiento con wish e if only.
  • La charla es clara, interesante y se ajusta al tiempo.

Glosario

If-clause
Parte de la oración que expresa la condición.
Main clause
Parte que expresa la consecuencia.
Unreal past
Pasado que expresa irrealidad, no tiempo pasado.
Second conditional
If + past, would + base: irreal en el presente.
Third conditional
If + past perfect, would have + participio: pasado imposible.
Mixed conditional
Mezcla de tiempos: pasado → presente o presente → pasado.
Were to
Hipótesis muy improbable: If it were to rain…
Unless
A menos que, si no.
Provided that
Siempre que, con la condición de que.
In case
Por si acaso.
Even if
Aunque (condición hipotética).
Conditional inversion
Condición sin if con el auxiliar delante: Had I known…
But for
Si no hubiera sido por.
Wish
Desear algo irreal o lamentar algo pasado.
Would rather
Preferir; con otro sujeto, + past simple.
It's high time
Ya es hora de (+ sujeto + past simple).

Tarjetas de repasoToca la tarjeta para darle la vuelta

Según cómo respondas, la tarjeta vuelve mañana, en 3, en 7 o en 21 días.

Para familias

  • Jugad en casa a «What would you do if…?» con preguntas imaginativas.
  • Contad en inglés una decisión familiar del pasado: «If we hadn't moved here…».
  • Escribid juntos tres deseos y tres arrepentimientos con I wish.
  • Repasad las tarjetas del tema cada noche durante una semana.

Para profesores

Saberes: Saberes básicos de Lengua Extranjera II (Inglés) de 2º de Bachillerato (RD 243/2022, BOE-A-2022-5521, bloques A. Comunicación, B. Plurilingüismo y C. Interculturalidad; en Cataluña, Decret 171/2022, Llengua Estrangera II), con la mirada puesta en la prueba de acceso a la universidad (PAU): funciones comunicativas de expresión de la condición, la hipótesis, el deseo, la preferencia, la queja y el arrepentimiento; oraciones condicionales reales, irreales, mixtas e invertidas; conectores condicionales (unless, provided that, as long as, in case, even if, otherwise); estructuras con pasado irreal (wish, if only, would rather, it's high time, as if); estrategias de cortesía y persuasión.

  • Debate «What if…?» sobre decisiones históricas con third conditional y mixtos.
  • Juego de cadenas condicionales: cada consecuencia es la condición de la frase siguiente.
  • Correos formales con inversión (Should you…) y fórmulas de cortesía.
  • Mural de deseos y arrepentimientos de la clase con wish e if only.

Fuentes y revisión

  • Real Decreto 243/2022, estructura y enseñanzas mínimas del Bachillerato (BOE)
  • Decret 171/2022, d'ordenació dels ensenyaments del batxillerat (DOGC)
  • British Council, LearnEnglish: B1-B2 and C1 grammar
  • Cambridge Dictionary, English Grammar Today
  • British Council, LearnEnglish: conditionals and wishes

Revisado el 21 de noviembre de 2026.

Qué vas a aprender

  • Dominar los cuatro tipos de condicionales y sus variantes con modales, formas continuas y were to
  • Construir condicionales mixtos en las dos direcciones (pasado → presente y presente → pasado)
  • Sustituir if por unless, provided that, as long as, in case, suppose, otherwise o even if
  • Usar la inversión condicional (Had I known, Should you need, Were it not for) y but for
  • Expresar deseos, quejas y arrepentimiento con wish, if only, would rather, it's time y as if
  • Resolver con seguridad las reescrituras condicionales de la PAU

Palabras clave

real vs unreal · were to · mixed conditionals · unless / provided that · in case / even if · inversion: had I known · should you need · but for / were it not for · wish + past / past perfect / would · if only · would rather + past · it's high time / as if

Tiempo

120 minutos hoy + 2 minutos en cada repaso
